title: Your First Weekend at Truman State University, Shared as Cards
description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented, trying campus spaces, and ending with a scheduled public program.

cards.entity_name: Ruth W. Towne Museum & Visitors Center
cards.title: Begin at the visitor center
cards.subtitle: First stop: Ruth W. Towne Museum & Visitors Center
cards.notes: Use the visitor center as a clear first landmark, then orient yourself with the campus map before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: Start with a named campus arrival point and map-listed destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s current campus map lists the Ruth W. Towne Museum & Visitors Center as destination 1.
cards.access_notes: Confirm visitor-center availability before making a special trip.

cards.title: Walk the Quad and locate your landmarks
cards.subtitle: Orientation loop: Quadrangle
cards.notes: Take an unhurried pass through the Quad, identifying Ophelia Parrish, Baldwin Hall, Kirk Memorial, and Pickler Memorial Library.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed central space for a self-guided campus orientation walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s campus map lists the Quadrangle and its Quad map labels Ophelia Parrish, Baldwin Hall, Kirk Memorial, and Pickler Memorial Library.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route; use sidewalks and adjust for weather.

cards.title: Make Pickler your reset point
cards.subtitle: Midday stop: Pickler Memorial Library
cards.notes: Find the service desk near the front doors, choose a seat, and save the library as a dependable place to return to.
cards.short_summary: A practical familiarization stop centered on the library’s main service point.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickler Memorial Library states that its Library Service Desk is near the front doors and that a Truman ID serves as a library card.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before arrival; borrowing requires a Truman ID.

cards.title: Pause at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Afternoon stop: Student Union Building
cards.notes: Walk through the building, note the conference-room area, and check posted involvement information for an event that fits your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed campus hub and base for Union and Involvement Services programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s campus map lists the Student Union, and Union and Involvement Services hosts multiple student events in the Student Union Building throughout the year.
cards.source_title: Student Appreciation Events – Union & Involvement Services
cards.access_notes: Building access and individual event availability vary; check current Union information.

cards.title: Choose a Student Activities Board event
cards.subtitle: Early-evening option: Student Activities Board
cards.notes: Check the SAB calendar or announcements, then pick one current program rather than planning around an assumed weekly event.
cards.short_summary: An adaptable campus-entertainment stop based on the current student-programming schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s Student Activities Board hosts regular semester programming including concerts, speakers, movie nights, DIYs, and seasonal festivals; most events are free for Truman students.
cards.source_title: Student Activities Board – Truman State University
cards.access_notes: Some programs require advance tickets or sign-ups because of capacity; verify the specific event before going.

cards.title: Try a low-key Rec Center session
cards.subtitle: Active break: Student Recreation Center
cards.notes: Use the walk/jog track or another available area for a short movement break, then check out before the facility closes.
cards.short_summary: A current-hours-backed campus recreation stop with a walk/jog track.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Recreation Center has an 11th-mile walk/jog track on its second floor and lists 2026 facility hours, including weekday evening availability.
cards.access_notes: Current listed hours: Monday–Thursday 6:30 a.m.–10 p.m.; Friday 6:30 a.m.–7 p.m.; weekends 11 a.m.–6 p.m. Confirm access requirements.

cards.title: See what is on view at the Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday cultural stop: Ophelia Parrish Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Check the exhibition dates first, then visit the gallery in Ophelia Parrish and give yourself time to look without rushing.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery with rotating faculty, student, and regional exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Art Gallery in Ophelia Parrish hosts faculty, student, art-historical, and regional contemporary exhibitions; exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The gallery is closed between exhibitions and during Truman breaks; the page lists Monday–Friday and Saturday hours.

cards.title: Locate the Pershing Natatorium
cards.subtitle: Campus facilities stop: Pershing Building
cards.notes: Find the natatorium on the campus map and check recreation information before planning a future swim or aquatic-program visit.
cards.short_summary: A named campus pool facility to add to your personal campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s campus map lists the Pershing Building Natatorium, and Truman describes a six-lane, 25-yard swimming pool among its recreation facilities.
cards.source_title: Fitness & Recreation at Truman State University
cards.access_notes: Pool schedules, access rules, and program availability should be confirmed with Campus Recreation.

cards.title: Plan a daytime look at University Farm
cards.subtitle: Off-campus-area stop: University Farm
cards.notes: Treat this as a separate daytime outing: review directions and current access first, then learn how the farm supports classes and recreation.
cards.short_summary: A 400-acre university property about 1.5 miles from campus with academic and recreational roles.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman describes University Farm as a 400-acre area about 1.5 miles from campus that supports classwork, research, and recreational opportunities.
cards.access_notes: It is about 1.5 miles from campus; confirm which areas are open and arrange transportation if needed.

cards.title: End with a scheduled stargazing night
cards.subtitle: Evening option: Truman State University Observatory
cards.notes: Use the observatory’s current stargazing schedule, dress for colder conditions, and follow its parking and walking directions after dark.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled public stargazing option at University Farm rather than an unscheduled late-night stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Truman State University Observatory publishes 2026 stargazing opportunities and states that it is located at University Farm on Boundary Street.
cards.access_notes: Attend only a listed session; the observatory directs visitors to park at the University Farm complex and walk up the short lane to the building.
